title: Samuel Asirvatham Raja vs Stella Janci Rani on 12 March, 2024

paragraphs.text:
C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 BEFORE THE MADURAI BENCH OF MADRAS HIGH COURT

 Dated: 12.03.2024
 CORAM:
 THE HON'BLE MR.JUSTICE P. DHANABAL


 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011
 and
 CMP(MD)No.6600 of 2017


 Samuel Asirvatham Raja .. Appellant/Petitioner


 Vs.


 Stella Janci Rani .. Respondent/Respondent



 Prayer : This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 55 of the

 Indian Divorce Act, against the judgment and decree dated 28.10.2010 in

 IDOP.No.47 of 2009 on the file of the I-Additional District Judge,

 Tirunelveli.



 For Appellant : Mr.T.A.Ebenezer
 For Respondent : Mr.S.Siva Thilakar


 1/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011



 JUDGMENT

This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellant as

 against the order passed by the I-Additional District Judge, Tirunelveli, in

 IDOP.No.47 of 2009 dated 28.10.2010 wherein the appellant herein has

 filed a petition seeking divorce on the ground of desertion as well as

 cruelty. The trial Court has dismissed the petition. As against the order

 passed by the trial Court, the present appeal is filed.

2. For the sake of convenience and brevity, the parties hereinafter

 will be referred to as per their status/ranking in the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner filed before the

 trial Court is as follows:

The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent was

 solemnized on 31.08.2005 at St. Paul's Church, NGO 'A' Colony,

 Tirunelveli. Out of the wedlock, a male child was born to them on

 01.08.2006. From the very date of marriage, the respondent was behaving

 abnormally. Further, by saying the trivial reasons, frequently, she has been


 2/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 going to her parental home at Tirunelveli and returned to the matrimonial

 home after the intervention of the elders of the family. In the course of

 time, the respondent began to spend more time in mobile phone. The

 petitioner later came to know that one Doctor from Tirunelveli having pre-

marital affairs with the respondent, still continuing his relationship with

 the respondent even after the marriage. The petitioner informed all the

 activities of the respondent's father. Even after the disclosure of the illegal

 contact to the family members, she did not repent for her conduct. The

 respondent living with her parents for more than six months in Tirunelveli

 with her son. The petitioner is subjected to mental and physical cruelty so

 far from his marriage with the respondent and hence, the petitioner is not

 willing to be subjected to such cruelty. Therefore, he filed a petition

 seeking for divorce.

4. The brief averments of the counter filed by the respondent

 before the trial Court are as follows:

According to the respondent, the respondent is an obedient wife of

 the petitioner and she was behaving in a normal manner. It is false to state

 that frequently the petitioner used to go to Tirunelveli on trivial reasons


 3/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 and returned back after the intervention of the elders of the family. The

 respondent has no such pre-marital affairs. It is scandalous allegation

 thrown on the respondent. The respondent was taking care of the family

 and child and she is obeying to the wishes of the petitioner. The petitioner

 suppressed the true facts and filed an application without any valid

 reasons. Though the petitioner was addicted to alcohol and used to abuse,

 beat and torture the respondent very often. In April 2008, she was tortured

 and beaten by the petitioner resulted in taking medical treatment and due

 to subsequent torture and cruelty caused by the petitioner, she

 administered with tablets for abortion on 07.01.2009 and thereafter, she

 was dropped in Tirunelveli by her in-laws on 09.01.2009. The petitioner

 has left the respondent in her parental home and with a view to abandon

 her, the respondent has also taken treatment in Tirunelveli. There is no

 mental and physical cruelty as against the petitioner. The respondent is

 always willing to have consortium and the petitioner alone has to change

 his connection with a girl by name Selvarani. Therefore, the divorce

 petition is liable to be dismissed.

5. Before the trial Court, in order to prove the case, on the side of


 4/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 the petitioner, he examined PW1 & PW2 and marked Ex.P1& Ex.P2. On

 the side of the respondent, she examined herself as RW1 and Ex.R1 to

 Ex.R4 were marked.

6. After evaluating the oral and documentary evidences adduced on

 either side, the tribunal has dismissed the petition on the ground that the

 petitioner has failed to prove the desertion as well as the cruelty.

 Aggrieved over the order passed by the trial Court, the petitioner has filed

 this appeal on the following grounds:

(1) The order of the Trial Court in dismissing the divorce petition is

 against the well settled principles of law and facts.

 (2) The learned trial Judge failed to consider the act of the respondent

 wife speaking with somebody else for day and night would cause

 mental cruelty to the husband.

(3) The trial Court wrongly come to a conclusion that the petitioner has

 not satisfactorily established the cruelty.

(4) The trial Court failed to consider the substantial mental cruelty

 suffered by the petitioner.

(5) The trial Court wrongly came to a conclusion that the petitioner



 5/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 having affairs with one Senthilrani by completely believing the

 version of the respondent.

(6) The trial Court failed to consider that she is making false allegation

 of illegal contact of the husband, she is causing more mental cruelty

 to him.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the

 marriage between the petitioner and the respondent was solemnized on

 31.08.2005 and a male child was born on 01.08.2006. After marriage, the

 respondent behaved abnormally and frequently, she left from the

 matrimonial home and stayed with her parents and the petitioner used to

 conduct panchayat and take back her to the matrimonial home. The

 respondent has affairs with one Doctor prior to marriage even now she is

 continuing her contact with the said Doctor through phone. Before the

 trial Court, in order to prove the case of the appellant, he examined

 himself as PW1 and he deposed about the mental cruelty caused by the

 respondent and the father of the petitioner was also examined as PW2. He

 also categorically deposed about the mental cruelty caused by the

 respondent. But the trial Court did not consider the above said evidence



 6/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 and wrongly came to a conclusion that the petitioner has not satisfactorily

 established the cruelty. However, the trial Court has given much

 importance to the evidence of the respondent's side and disbelieved the

 evidence of the petitioner's side and therefore, the order passed by the trial

 Court is liable to be set aside by allowing this appeal.

8. The learned counsel for the respondent would contend that the

 petitioner filed a petition on the ground of desertion and cruelty. In the

 said petition itself, the petitioner pleaded that for the past six months, the

 respondent deserted the petitioner. To attract the grounds under Section

 10(9) of the Divorce Act, the petitioner has to prove that the respondent

 deserted the petitioner for atleast two years. But the petitioner has filed to

 prove the ground of desertion. As far as the cruelty is concerned, no

 sufficient evidence adduced by the petitioner to prove the cruelty. He made

 allegations as against the respondent that the respondent has illicit

 intimacy with a Doctor and there is no evidence to prove that and not even

 mentioned the name of the Doctor. Per contra, the respondent's side

 evidence shows that the petitioner only had illicit relationship with one

 Senthilrani and the same was suppressed in his petition. When the



 7/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 petitioner only caused cruelty to the respondent but still the respondent is

 ready to live with the petitioner. In order to prove the case of the

 respondent, she examined herself as RW1 and marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.

 The trial Court, after considering the evidence, correctly came to a

 conclusion and dismissed the petition filed by the petitioner. Therefore,

 the present appeal filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed.

9. This Court has considered the submission made by either side

 counsel and perused the materials available on record.
(i)Whether the appeal is liable to be allowed or not?

11. In this case, there is no dispute regarding the relationship

 between the parties and the male child born to the parties. The appellant

 has filed the petition before the trial Court for the decree of divorce on the

 ground of desertion as well as cruelty. As far as the ground of desertion is



 8/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 concerned, the petitioner himself admitted in the petition that the

 respondent has been residing with her parents for more than six months.

 But to attract the grounds under Section 10(9) of the Divorce Act, the

 petitioner has to prove that the respondent has deserted the petitioner for

 atleast two years from the date of petition. But there is no sufficient

 evidence adduced by the petitioner and he himself admitted through the

 pleadings that for more than six months, the respondent has been residing

 with her parents. Therefore, the ground of desertion has not been proved

 by the petitioner. As far as the cruelty is concerned, according to the

 petitioner, the respondent behaved abnormally and there is no particular

 incident stated by the petitioner in respect of the abnormal behaviour. In

 this context, PW1 and PW2 were examined on the side of the petitioner

 and they have deposed about the happenings in the family.

12. The main contention of the appellant/petitioner is that the

 respondent frequently gone to her parent's house and she had illicit

 intimacy with one Doctor. The petitioner failed to prove the abnormal

 behaviour and also failed to prove the intimacy with one Doctor. There is

 no evidence to prove the alleged abnormal behaviour. The petitioner in the



 9/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

 petition not even stated about the kind of abnormal behaviour and also not

 even mentioned the name of the Doctor and without any evidence and

 records, he levelled allegations against the respondent. In this context, the

 trial Court, in the order, has elaborately discussed about the admission

 made by PW1 and PW2 in the cross-examination that the respondent's

 possession of pills for abortion and the illegal intimacy with one

 Senthilrani, and thereafter, dismissed the petition.

13. On perusal of the entire records shows that the evidence

 adduced on the petitioner's side, there is no sufficient material to prove the

 grounds raised by the petitioner in the application. Therefore, this Court is

 of the opinion that the petitioner has failed to prove the allegation levelled

 against the petitioner and failed to prove the grounds of desertion as well

 as cruelty. The trial Court also elaborately discussed about the evidences

 adduced by either side and came to a fair conclusion. Therefore, the order

 passed by the trial Court is in order and there is no infirmity and perversity

 of the order passed by the trial Court. Accordingly, this appeal has no

 merits and fails.

10/12
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 C.M.A.(MD)No.89 of 2011

14. In view of the above discussion, this Civil Miscellaneous

 Appeal is dismissed. No Costs. Consequently, connected miscellaneous

 petition is closed.
